name: 21401-longctxdecode-granite4tiny-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. A 7B bf16 checkpoint fits one card.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1, bounded at 24 requests / 900 s safety, warmup the first 25% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, prompt EXACTLY 31500 tokens and output EXACTLY 512 (min = max, so the backend forces ignore_eos), prefix caching off. Wire length is not declared length: the chat template plus re-tokenization put the engine's own prompt-token count somewhat above 31500, and max-model-len 32768 carries the slack.
purpose: A long-document analysis assistant summarizing 30,000-word briefs into page-long answers for one user at a time on a single GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 42172ad18fbc22c89d0063184e4570cc84186e16 (v0.10.0-502-g42172ad18fbc).
# Interpreter and hardware seal live in configs/env.yaml, which is per-machine and NOT portable.

model: ibm-granite/granite-4.0-tiny-preview
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The checkpoint's config.json declares no `torch_dtype`; `auto` reads bf16 off the safetensors
# metadata. Written out so the resolution needs no network and cannot drift.
dtype: bfloat16

max-model-len: 32768

# PINNED rather than left to resolve: entering through `AsyncLLMEngine.from_engine_args` at this
# commit falls through to the scheduler's own defaults (2048 batched tokens, 128 seqs), which
# would cut the 31,500-token prompt into 16 scheduler steps instead of 2.
max-num-batched-tokens: 16384
max-num-seqs: 1024

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# MANDATORY HERE, not a preference: at this commit GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM raises at
# construction if prefix caching is on.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# The attention backend is not an AsyncEngineArgs field on this engine -- it is selected by
# VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND, so the FlashInfer pin is realised in configs/tuned.yaml `apply:`.
